records.question: Is cosmetic surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: Are claims for self-inflicted injury or suicide attempt payable under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What maternity benefit coverage is provided under Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: Under what condition is dental treatment covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Dental treatment or surgery is covered only when it requires hospitalization that arises solely from an accidental injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are weight loss treatments and bariatric surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: Are hospital admissions primarily for diagnostic evaluations covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the cumulative bonus percentage increase per claim-free year under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the Pre-existing Disease definition time window on Page 1 correspond to the PED waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The definition of a Pre‑existing Disease (PED) on Page 1 states that a condition is considered pre‑existing if it was present, diagnosed, or treated within **36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
On Page 3, the waiting period for a Pre‑existing Disease is also **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the time window used to define a PED matches exactly the waiting period that must elapse before a claim for a pre‑existing condition becomes admissible.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the initial waiting period for day care procedures on Page 2 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The initial waiting period for day‑care procedures is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
This is identical to the general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury), which is also **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the organ donor limit in the benefits table on Page 2 align with the organ donor support clause on Page 6?
records.answer:
The benefits table on Page 2 lists the organ donor expense limit as “Covered up to Rs. 2,00,000 per policy year” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The Organ Donor Expense Support clause on Page 6 states that “Hospitalisation expenses incurred for organ donation harvesting from a living donor are payable up to an enhanced limit of Rs. 2,00,000” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].  

Thus, both the table and the clause specify the same monetary ceiling of Rs. 2,00,000 for organ‑donor related expenses, confirming that the limits are aligned.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the cataract surgery waiting period in the table on Page 3, and what sub-limit is specified in Clause 3.4 on Page 3 and Page 2?
records.answer:
The cataract surgery waiting period listed in the table on Page 3 is **12 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
Clause 3.4 on Page 3 specifies a **cataract sub‑limit of Rs. 60,000 per eye** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Page 2 does not contain a separate cataract sub‑limit; the only sub‑limits on that page relate to room rent, ICU/ICCU charges, etc.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the accidental bodily injury exception to the waiting period on Page 3 relate to the reconstructive cosmetic surgery clause on Page 4?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, the waiting‑period rule on page 3 exempts accidental bodily injury from the 30‑day waiting period that applies to all other illnesses. This means that if a claim arises from an accidental bodily injury, the 30‑day waiting period does not apply.  

On page 4, the policy states that cosmetic or aesthetic surgery is excluded **unless** it is a reconstructive procedure required after an accidental bodily injury. Because accidental bodily injury is exempt from the waiting period, a reconstructive cosmetic surgery performed after such an injury is covered without the 30‑day waiting period.  

Thus, the accidental‑bodily‑injury exception to the waiting period allows reconstructive cosmetic surgery following an accidental injury to be paid immediately, whereas other cosmetic procedures remain excluded.  

[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the maternity benefit waiting period under Section 4.3 on Page 4 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The maternity benefit under Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 requires a **24‑month waiting period** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  
By contrast, the general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what notice is required for planned admission on Page 5, and what minimum hospital stay is required on Page 1?

The policy requires that the insured or their representative give notice **at least 48 hours prior to a planned admission** at a network hospital [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].  
The minimum hospital stay that constitutes inpatient hospitalisation is a **continuous period of 24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the Free-Look Period duration defined on Page 1, and what refund terms apply under Section 5.3 on Page 5?
records.answer:
The Free‑Look Period is defined as **15 days** from the date of receipt of the policy document by the policyholder [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Section 5.3 on Page 5, if no claim is made during that period, the premium is refunded **subject to minimal administrative charges** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: How do the ICU charges limits differ between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
